label: Turn a skill and a brief into a live site
job: Use any available skill, tool or creative method with a brief to build a reusable site or interactive app, publish it at a live trillion.run link, inspect the actual result, and keep the reusable method in the Trillion marketplace. Supports both new sites and edits to the same installation.

skill_source.description: A Marketplace workflow id, public repository or skill URL, or an available skill/file reference. Do not put a credential here.

installation_id.description: When editing, keep this installation and its data/history.

source_owner.description: Existing owned repository/project or saved Sites project; discover it when omitted.

source.from: completed work generalized into a reusable method
source.note: The method preserves live hosting, same-origin scripts, licensed source, comparable visual proof, retries and saved workflow execution. Example-specific copy, credentials and installation identities are inputs, never instructions.

steps.title: Load the skill and define the result
steps.do: Read the brief and skill_source. Use find_workflow and describe_workflow for an existing method before creating a duplicate. Otherwise read the actual source and support files, pin the source revision, resolve license and redistribution permission, and keep attribution. Discover the existing product/source owner and use its supported build/hosting actions. Trillion is standalone: never attach its work to a retired runtime. Use the selected customer AI; do not silently substitute a provider. Describe the promised visitor behavior and the required success checks, including all expected_behaviors. For missing capability, discover or extend the smallest shared owner. Keep credentials with their owner and out of the site and workflow. A failed transport is not a missing credential. Do not ask routine approvals already covered by the request.

checks.says: The resolved brief keeps the actual requested outcome.

steps.title: Build from reusable parts
steps.do: Apply the actual skill to this run's brief. Build behavior in shared UI/components and appearance in the shared look owner; callers supply data and copy. Keep the generator, data, dependency/license references and a repeatable build command with the source owner. Never author executable source in an instruction/history folder. For an existing installation, first read its revision and retain an authentic live baseline. Keep the same installation and data; use revision-checked edits, not a replacement site. New work records that no earlier baseline exists. Produce a site files map or saved site-file identity with index.html. Serve animation/behavior as same-origin JS files: the host enforces CSP; never weaken it or rely on blocked inline scripts. Avoid fabricated business results or live feeds. Add genuine backend/visitor actions only when the brief needs them, through the existing declared owners. Worker modules must be self-contained, from pinned source and the supported source manifest; the site host does not run repository build scripts.

checks.says: The build covers each promised behavior.
The site contains an entry page.

steps.title: Check the complete preview
steps.do: Build and open the real preview with one browser at a time. Inspect the whole page at phone and desktop widths, all collection kinds, first/middle/last items where applicable, keyboard/focus, reduced motion, actual interaction and console errors. Use the chosen skill's own geometry/craft checks where applicable. Verify actual media previews, links and declared visitor actions; placeholders and an HTTP 200 are insufficient. For each promised operation, check successful use and relevant denial/retry behavior without deleting real user data. Fix every found issue through the shared owner. Preserve genuine screenshots/recording and a complete checked file manifest. A not-applicable check needs a domain reason. Do not publish an unfinished preview as ready.

checks.says: The preview covers all six required inspection areas.

steps.title: Publish through Trillion and keep the address
steps.do: Discover the live public-app tool schemas rather than copying obsolete payloads. For a new site call publish_public_app_definition with id=input.app_id, the checked files or files_from, and actual actions (an empty list for an illustrative site). Call install_public_app with the returned version, input.context (private when omitted), a stable installation_id for safe retries, and input.site_name. Keep the installation response and live URL. For edits use read_public_app_installation, write_public_app_file/edit_public_app_draft with fresh revisions, then publish_public_app_draft; keep the same installation, address, database and version history. Rename only through name_public_app. Attach/enable a backend only through the supported source owner when needed. A timeout after mutation is an unknown result: read back the known app/installation before retrying. Never generate a second installation to hide a failed read. Preserve recovery evidence. Return the actual live owner response, not a guessed URL.

steps.title: Exercise the actual hosted result
steps.do: Read the installation and fetch the live URL and every required script/asset/route. Compare the actual served content with the checked manifest, allowing only documented host transforms. Repeat the promised visitor behavior on the hosted page: complete desktop and phone page, keyboard/focus, reduced-motion stillness, real motion/interaction, themes if present and no uncaught page errors. Check backend/visitor actions against the owning records when present. Capture fresh comparable after visuals and label changes without fabricating pixels; retain the authentic baseline or say none existed. Use a short real screen recording for motion. An uploaded definition, installed row, loading shell or passing route is not completion. Fix CSP/asset/action/layout failures and republish through the same installation until the live outcome passes; if a real external boundary remains, retain it and do not submit a successful result.

checks.says: The hosted page passes the complete inspection.
Every promised behavior is verified live.
The checked page is the published installation.

steps.title: Keep the skill, reusable method and final result
steps.do: Keep the skill findable with license and pinned support-file retrieval: use skill_repositories for a shareable public source or save_workflow for an admissible skill recipe. For global visibility publish the same saved workflow identity with publish_workflow; an account-only source registration is not global publication. Do not duplicate an existing source/workflow. This generic workflow is the shared end-to-end method; improve it in place only for a reusable discovery. Save output-specific methods only when they add a distinct reusable job. Remove example URLs, private facts, paths and secrets from every globally published recipe. Keep the built source in the right repository/project, land source through that owner's supported API with a fresh expected-head lease when applicable, and independently read back the exact bytes. Read describe_workflow and find_workflow to verify findability, declared inputs and all steps; record global publish separately from a separate-account/UI check, which must never be invented. Return the actual live URL, workflow/skill references and real screenshots/video in plain language. A native-tool job without run_tool task records must explicitly save/publish its generic method; learn_workflow cannot infer work it never recorded.

checks.says: The final link names the verified installation.
